name: Two-tone headline pair (statement, then counterpoint)

source.description: 10 inspected reference films (batch-2, batch-4, batch-5, batch-6, batch-7, 2026-11-26): several product and brand films set a two-line headline in which line 2 answers line 1 in the accent colour (or grey), section after section.

technique: A two-line headline in which the first line states and the second answers or turns, set in the accent colour (or a lighter grey) and arriving a beat later. The colour split shows where the payoff is without a highlight effect, and repeated per section it becomes the film's headline grammar.
purpose: Show where a headline's payoff is without a highlight effect; repeated per section it becomes the film's headline grammar.
visual_behaviour: Line 1 states in the body colour; a beat later line 2 answers in the accent colour or a lighter grey, at the same size and weight.
mechanics: Line 1 in the body colour, line 2 in the accent (or about 50% grey for a quieter contrast), same size and weight; words fade or rise in about 0.07-0.1 s apart; line 2 starts 0.15-0.5 s after line 1, or on the next accent. Left-aligned beside a proof card, or centred.

decomposition.timing: Headline complete in about 0.3-0.6 s; one pair per section of about 2-3 s.

use_cases: Section openers beside a proof card
failure_modes: Using the accent on every line 2 and elsewhere too dilutes it
A line 2 longer than line 1 loses the punch

implementation.approach: Studio.comp.headline(parent, {line1, line2}) (runtime 1.18.0, preset pair): line 2 in the accent (or muted), same size; words rise 0.08 s apart; line 2 starts lineDelay after line 1's stagger or at line2At (a spoken word); warns when line 2 is longer than line 1.

requirements: two text lines with an accent class

provenance.observed: Seven sections each open with a black line and an ultramarine second line ('Every project. / One link.'), words about 0.07-0.1 s apart.
'Discover / new music' and 'Find your rhythm' with the second line in green, each landing on an accent.
'Pay anyone. / Anywhere.' and 'In seconds. / Not days.' with the second line in grey, landing on the next accent.

The opening serif headline sets line 1 first (1.27 s) and adds an italic terracotta line 2 (2.11 s); later headlines keep the grammar with an italic terracotta phrase (29.95, 48.52 s). Read from the overview sheet by the integrator.
A two-line headline whose line 2 is set in the accent blue and arrives after line 1 (1.13-1.88 s); the closing headline repeats the pattern (33.43 s). Read from the overview sheet by the integrator.
Variant with one accent word instead of a whole accent line: line 1 white, line 2 ends on an italic serif word in red (0.4-1.1 s; 8.27-8.50 s); words 0.1-0.2 s apart.

Light-canvas launch: every claim is two lines left of the interface, line 2 ending on the key word in an accent colour (red for the problem 2.40 s, blue for a feature 18.80 s, teal for the promise 41.97 s); words blur in a fixed 0.13 s apart, the accent word last.
Heavy caps pairs on dark navy: line 2 in red for the problem (3.38 s) and in blue for each promise (4.88, 6.38, 10.89, 12.39 s), 1-3 words per line, about 2 s each.
Each feature headline is two lines, a white statement then a violet payoff arriving about 0.1 s later (3.27/3.37 s, 9.35 s, 11.35 s).
Headlines put the payoff half in orange: 'their product' (3.4 s), 'they buy' (7.1 s), the second line of the end card (13.1 s).
